solutionMathEvidence: Adults one each on A,B,C have 3!=6 placements. With residual capacities 1,2,2, child placements are 6 when A is empty (B/C split one and two), plus 12 when one child rides A (choose that child in 3 ways, then assign each other child to B or C in 2^2 ways), giving 6·18=108. If A is empty and adults split 1 and 2 between B,C, choose the one-adult ride in 2 ways, its adult in 3 ways, and the child using the single remaining seat in 3 ways, giving 18. Other adult patterns cannot fit all three children under the capacities and adult-presence rule. Thus 108+18=126, answer ③.
